title: Legacy history can stay stale after a completed Showdown is archived
steps: Open Legacy once before the Showdown is finished, with 0 completed Showdowns, so the in-memory Legacy list and rendered revision both represent 0 records.
Play a normal 1-season Showdown and finish it 5-3 overall. The season completion path saves the completed Showdown and runtimeArchiveShowdown writes the completed record into Legacy.
Open Legacy again without reloading the app.
Because the runtime archive write does not invalidate storage.js's Legacy cache or advance its Legacy revision, renderLegacy can reuse the old rendered revision or load the stale cached list.
expected: Legacy immediately shows 1 completed Showdown, the 5-3 final score, and its Season 1 history.
actual: Legacy can still show the earlier 0-showdown view until the app is reloaded or another path invalidates the Legacy cache.
root_cause: Legacy history has an in-memory cache and render revision in storage.js/legacy.js, but Save Library runtime writes to the same Legacy history in the same page without invalidating that cache or advancing the revision. Same-page writes do not receive the browser storage event used for cross-tab invalidation.
checked_against: js/seasonEngine.js persistCompletedSeason saves the completed Showdown before calling archiveShowdown.
js/legacy.js archiveCompletedSaveBeforeLegacy retries missing archives, but it begins from loadLegacyShowdowns and therefore can consult the stale cache.
js/saveLibraryRuntime.js runtimeArchiveShowdown avoids duplicate records by Showdown id and revision, so duplicate history is not the problem.
js/storage.js saveLegacyShowdowns does advance the cache revision, but runtimeArchiveShowdown does not use that function.

fix.change: Give same-page Save Library runtime writes that change Legacy history a shared cache-invalidation hook, and call it after every successful Legacy-changing transaction so the next History render reads the new record and revision.

assumptions: Normal local play is being checked; no account, device, network, or remote-history behavior is included.
Legacy was opened at least once before the Showdown was completed, which is a normal navigation path.
No page reload occurs between finishing the Showdown and reopening Legacy.
